answers.text: Same as before with the driver text — I'd say three lines, same order every time: drop-off time, pallet count, then damage noted. That keeps it the same each time you run it.
For the call logs, I'd just say list the customer and the topic for each call, one line each.
Looking at this again, access from 8am, six hours needed, but it says finishing on the 23rd. Something about that timing feels wrong to me. I'd get it checked before filing.
The on-time rate at 92% seems right based on 9 out of 118. I looked at the increase from 96 to 118 too, roughly 20-something percent, hard to say exactly without working it out properly.
I'd pick Output 2, reads better and sounds more thorough to a client.
I'd go with Email 2, it just seems like the stronger one to send.

1. Vendor's pricing — yes, normal to share in a quote summary. 2. Total spend, aggregate — yes, no vendor names attached so it's fine. 3. Unsigned budget draft — no, that's not settled or released yet. 4. Datasheet already published — yes, it's already public on their site. 5. Employee's home address — no, that's personal information.
The rates and retainer cap I'd hold back from pasting directly in, too sensitive without a cleared tool. The NDA clause too, since it names both companies. Not sure about the rest of it.
Before it goes out, I check the totals against the warehouse system numbers. Same thing every month before sending it on.

Step 1 carries risk, if the invoice details get read wrong there it carries through. But step 4 is really the one that matters, since it gets approved and paid automatically without anyone checking first. I'd put a gate there.
